candidates.title: Path-Compressed Trie for Efficient KV Cache Reuse
candidates.venue: International Conference on Communication, Computing & Security
candidates.abstract: In Large Language Models (LLMs), prefix matching in the sequences of requests is a critical issue. It can improve inference efficiency by reusing the results of previous computations. The key tensors and the value tensors in the KV cache are computed using the sequences of requests, and our goal is to find the co-prefixed part in these sequences. However, existing prefix matching approaches store all prefix parts of each sequence in a hash table, which encounter significant challenges in efficiently matching reusable KV cache due to the need for multiple memory accesses. In this paper, we present a novel triebased approach for indexing request sequences, wherein our path compression technique substantially minimizes memory accesses required for matching. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves the match performance by $2.11 \times$ compared with matching strategy in Mooncake.
candidates.reason: 経路圧縮トライでリクエスト系列の接頭辞を索引化しKVキャッシュ再利用のための接頭辞マッチングのメモリアクセスを減らす手法で、Mooncake比2.11倍のマッチ性能を示すKVキャッシュ機構である

candidates.title: Scrooge: Accelerating Attention Inference in LLMs via Early Termination Mechanism
candidates.venue: Design, Automation and Test in Europe
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in natural language processing and are now widely adopted in diverse applications. However, their significant computation and memory costs severely limit their acceleration. In particular, the self-attention mechanism is a significant bottleneck, as it cannot exploit batch parallelism across prompts, and its memory traffic grows quadratically with sequence length. In this paper, we propose Scrooge, a novel hardware accelerator framework that leverages an attention early termination mechanism, designed to address the inefficiency of self-attention. The self-attention mechanism does not assign equal importance to all tokens. Instead, semantically important tokens consistently receive higher attention scores. Consequently, preserving sufficient attention for a subset of important tokens is often enough to maintain model accuracy, even without computing attention for all tokens. Our key insight is that once sufficient attention has been accumulated, further computation with the remaining tokens only increases complexity without improving accuracy. Scrooge leverages this insight to approximate the attention of the remaining tokens and terminates the attention computation dynamically once it has gathered sufficient attention. With this method, Scrooge reduces both latency and memory traffic while maintaining accuracy. Experimental results show that Scrooge achieves a 1.7× speedup and a 0.47× reduction in memory traffic with negligible accuracy loss.
candidates.reason: Scroogeは注意の累積が十分になった時点で残りトークンの注意計算を早期終了・近似するハードウェア加速機構で、注意推論のレイテンシ1.7倍高速化とメモリトラフィック削減を実現する

candidates.title: Collaborative Multi-Device Edge Inference for Vision-Language Models with Speculative Decoding
candidates.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Personal, Indoor and Mobile Radio Communications
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable success across various domains. However, the substantial computational and memory demands pose significant challenges for deploying LLMs at the network edge. To address this issue, the existing studies mainly focus on either reducing the size of LLMs or distributing LLMs across multiple devices. However, the former approach suffers from performance degradation, while the latter incurs high communication cost due to the transmission of high-dimensional intermediate features. To tackle these issues, we propose a novel collaborative framework to support vision-language model (VLM) inference at the network edge, expanding speculative decoding into a multi-device scenario. In this framework, each edge device first utilizes its small VLM to generate draft tokens in an auto-regressive manner. These tokens are then transmitted to an edge server, where they are corrected in parallel by a large VLM. By benefiting from speculative decoding, the number of calls to the large VLM is reduced without degrading the inference performance. Furthermore, we minimize the average latency of inference tasks by developing a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to optimize the number of draft tokens generated at each iteration. Simulation results confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves a lower average latency compared to other baselines.
candidates.reason: 複数エッジデバイスの小規模VLMがドラフトトークンを生成し投機的デコードを多デバイス協調へ拡張する枠組みで、通信コストを抑えながらエッジでのVLM推論を高速化する分散推論手法である

candidates.title: Leveraging Expert Usage to Speed up LLM Inference with Expert Parallelism
candidates.abstract: —Large language models have become indispensable for many text-processing applications. Their inference, i.e. their use to generate text, is a time-consuming task since tokens have to be generated one after the other, even if the computational load has been reduced by model sparsification, e.g. by using a Mixture of Experts (MoE) models. In the MoE context, a subset of experts is selected at each stage. Note that not all subsets of experts (pairs of experts in most cases) in a given layer have the same probability of being selected. When experts are mapped to different GPUs, there is a risk of load imbalance if the selected experts end up on a small number of GPUs. This paper proposes to leverage this heterogeneity in expert usage to map experts of popular subsets onto distinct GPUs, allowing them to be processed in parallel and thus reducing the time needed for inference. Even though this mapping problem is NP-complete, it is possible to design simple greedy strategies that significantly reduce the need for sequential expert processing. Our proof-of-concept confirms that our mapping strategies effectively reduce inference time on the Mixtral model.
candidates.reason: MoE推論で共起頻度の高いエキスパートペアを別GPUへ配置するエキスパート並列マッピングを提案し、負荷不均衡による逐次処理を減らしてMixtralの推論時間を削減する分散推論最適化である

candidates.title: ESWD: Entropy-Stratified Sliding-Window Decoding for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models due to their potential for parallel text generation. However, their inference efficiency is often constrained by decoding strategies that restrict parallel decoding to fixed token blocks, leading to unstable parallelism during generation. We propose <bold>ESWD</bold>, a training-free decoding strategy for efficient diffusion language model inference. ESWD first introduces a sliding-window candidate selection mechanism that dynamically maintains a stable set of masked positions while preserving semi-autoregressive ordering. On this basis, ESWD further applies an entropy-stratified parallel decoding strategy that aggressively decodes low-entropy tokens in parallel, while selectively resolving high-entropy decisions through entropy-guided exploration to control error propagation. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that ESWD achieves <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2.2\times$</tex-math></inline-formula>–<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$5.0\times$</tex-math></inline-formula> speedup over standard decoding baselines while maintaining comparable or improved generation quality.
candidates.reason: ESWDは拡散言語モデル向けにスライディングウィンドウ候補選択とエントロピー層別並列デコードを組み合わせ、学習なしで標準デコード比2.2〜5.0倍の高速化を示す直接的なデコード効率化手法である
